newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVENERGO GENERATORS IN SELL-OFF BY CHRISTMAS.
newsitem.headline: LATVENERGO GENERATORS IN SELL-OFF BY CHRISTMAS.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) said on Wednesday that Latvenergo's generating companies may be partly privatised by Christmas.
It also said that Latvenergo, the state elctricity firm currently being prepared for sell-off, should start operating as a holding company from July 1.
"It is desirable that Latvenergo starts functioning as a holding company with daughter firms and separate costs centres from July 1," Janis Naglis, LPA general director, told a news conference.
The LPA earlier said January 1, 1998 was the date for Latvenergo to start operating as a holding firm.
Privatisation guidelines provide for four electricity generating firms to be set up with the grid forming a separate firm and acting only as buyer.
"I expect that the generation side of Latvenergo could be poartly privatised by Christmas," Naglis said.
Two generators on the Daugava river, Plavinas and Kegums hydro-electric power stations, are to form one generating firm while Riga hydro-electric station would constitute the other.
Two more companies will be set up from the thermal power stations TEC-1 and TEC-2.
